themes.thesis: Miners rallying hard — 167-name cohort up +6.6% median, led by Century Aluminum's post-earnings surge and fresh copper-project financing headlines.
themes.rationale: The 167-ticker mining cohort posted a +6.6% median 3-day reaction, the strongest of any sector this window (2,629 news items in 14 days). Century Aluminum (CENX US) rallied +13.6% and Taseko Mines (TGB US) +8.8% after their Q2 prints. Meanwhile Ivanhoe Electric (IE US) is mapping a $1B debt path for its Arizona copper project and Hudbay (HBM US) is being framed as building a copper giant after filing an early warning report on Panoro Minerals — both signs of active portfolio-building inside the group even as IE US itself pulled back -3.3%.

themes.thesis: Alt-asset managers mostly higher post-earnings — Ares up +6%, Blackstone +4.4%, but Apollo bucks the trend at -4.6%.
themes.rationale: The 6-name alternative-asset-management cohort posted a +2.9% median 3-day reaction on 231 news items. Ares Management (ARES US) led with +6.0% and Blackstone (BX US) added +4.4%, with KKR (KKR US) and Brookfield (BN US) also positive at +3.1% and +2.7%. Apollo Global Management (APO US) was the outlier, down -4.6% despite reporting in the same window. Filing activity was heavy across the group — KKR alone generated four separate Form 4s and an 8-K in the two weeks after its print, while Brookfield filed a 6-K and an N-PX.

themes.thesis: Industrials are beating estimates but selling off anyway — 576-name cohort's median surprise is +4.3% yet the median reaction is -1.5%.
themes.rationale: Across the 576-ticker industrials cohort (6,810 news items, the thickest window of any sector), the median earnings surprise was a solid +4.28% — yet the median 3-day reaction was still -1.5%, a classic sell-the-news pattern. Individual moves were far more extreme: Samsung SDI plunged -53% and Ecopro -52% on their Q1 prints. Meanwhile a steady wave of Form 4 filings hit real-name industrials this week — Rocket Lab (RKLB US), Axon (AXON US), and Eaton (ETN US) among them — consistent with post-earnings insider trading windows opening across the group.
